o.text: Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish آزْ (az), from Proto-Turkic *āŕ.
From Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (böl-, “to separate”), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *bȫl- (“to divide, separate, distinguish”). Cognate with Turkish bölmek, etc.

Inherited from Proto-Common Turkic *xātun (“queen, lady”). The form in the standard language was likely reintroduced by intellectuals influenced by the Ottoman language around 1900 after a few centuries of disuse (see the quotation from 1914).
From Persian نقطه نظر. Compare Turkmen nukdaýnazar.
From a derivation of Proto-Turkic *yal- (“name of different types of grass”). Cognate with Turkish yarpuz.
